approaches.title: Iterative paired-stack traversal
approaches.summary: Traverses both trees iteratively while pairing corresponding nodes on a stack. It checks null structure and node values together.

revisions.shortChangeSummary: Uses separate stacks for the two trees and compares corresponding nodes during traversal.

revisions.rawCommitSubject: rust 100: single stack & better pattern matching
revisions.shortChangeSummary: Refactors to one stack of paired nodes and uses pattern matching to handle null and non-null cases.

approaches.title: Recursive tree comparison
approaches.summary: Recursively compares corresponding nodes and their left and right subtrees. It passes references to the existing reference-counted node handles instead of cloning them for traversal.

revisions.commitComment: recursive is cleaner and makes no heap allocations & no reference counting
revisions.rawCommitSubject: rust 100: recursive is cleaner and makes no heap allocations & no reference counting
revisions.commitBody:
- recursion operates on the call stack, thus not requiring a heap
allocated vector to track the node stack

- recursion preserves the lifetime of the owning nodes, allowing
children nodes to be passed down by a reference to their reference
handle (Rc) rather than cloning the reference handle which incurs
counting overhead and the Rc destructor checking if the strong_count is
0 to clean up the underlying heap node
revisions.shortChangeSummary: Replaces the explicit stack with a recursive helper that compares values and recursively checks both child pairs.
